VNET Group.why: Chinese wholesale hyperscale data-center operator leasing AI-driven capacity to cloud and internet companies; 862 MW of new wholesale orders year-to-date 2026 and 1,007 MW in service
VNET Group.evidence: VNET Group Q2 FY2026 call (08-18-2026), Rotating President Wen Teng: 'we won a new 345 MW wholesale order in the second quarter from a leading cloud service provider for our data center in the Greater Beijing Area'; 'our wholesale capacity in service rose by 49.4% year-over-year to 1,007 MW'

players.product: Wholesale hyperscale IDC in China (Greater Beijing / Ulanqab campuses) leased to cloud and internet companies, plus retail IDC; 1,007 MW wholesale capacity in service as of June 30, 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026: total net revenues RMB 2.78 billion, up 14.2% YoY; wholesale revenues RMB 1.10 billion, up 29.3% and 39.8% of total revenue (again above retail); retail revenues RMB 1.05 billion, up 9.1%; non-IDC revenues RMB 628.4 million, up 1.1%. Adjusted EBITDA RMB 918.3 million, up 25.4%, margin 33.0% (30.1% a year ago); adjusted cash gross margin 41.8% (43.6% a year ago) on higher pass-through utility costs; adjusted net income RMB 7.4 million versus a loss a year ago.
quarterly_data.figure: net revenues RMB 2.78 billion (+14.2% YoY); wholesale RMB 1.10 billion (+29.3%); adjusted EBITDA RMB 918.3 million (+25.4%)

quarterly_data.signal: Orders: 347 MW of new orders in Q2, including a new 345 MW wholesale order from a leading cloud service provider for a Greater Beijing Area data center and about 2 MW of retail orders. Four wholesale orders total 862 MW year-to-date 2026 (the 345 MW plus 517 MW announced last quarter); among them, a 510 MW order was signed with a leading internet company. Reservations stood at 355 MW, taking total orders and reservations to over 1.2 GW; management says all customer reservations have historically converted into firm orders. Delivery schedule for the 862 MW: approximately 287 MW in 2026, 345 MW in 2027 and 230 MW in 2028 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 new orders 347 MW; 862 MW wholesale orders YTD; 355 MW reservations; orders + reservations over 1.2 GW

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity as of June 30, 2026: wholesale capacity in service 1,007 MW (up 49.4% YoY, first time above 1 GW), 96.3% committed by customers; utilized 744 MW (up 45.5%), utilization 73.9%, mature-capacity utilization 92.5%. Capacity under construction 585 MW with a 94.2% pre-commitment rate; about 1.1 GW held for future development, mainly Greater Beijing. Total wholesale resource capacity over 4 GW, up approximately 1.5 GW QoQ, of which the newly secured land bank supports approximately 1.4 GW (908 MW in the Chinese mainland, mainly Inner Mongolia and East China, and 478 MW overseas). Retail: 50,081 cabinets in service, utilization 64.5%, MRR per cabinet RMB 9,799.
quarterly_data.figure: 1,007 MW in service (+49.4% YoY); 744 MW utilized (73.9%); 585 MW under construction (94.2% pre-committed); over 4 GW wholesale resource

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance reiterated (SVP Peter Zhang): total net revenues RMB 11.5 billion-RMB 11.8 billion (+15.6%-18.6% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA RMB 3.55 billion-RMB 3.75 billion (+19.2%-25.9% YoY). Capex was RMB 3.55 billion in H1 2026, and full-year 2026 capex is still expected at RMB 10 billion-RMB 12 billion, mainly to support planned delivery of 450 MW-500 MW in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue RMB 11.5 billion-RMB 11.8 billion; adjusted EBITDA RMB 3.55 billion-RMB 3.75 billion; capex RMB 10 billion-RMB 12 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Delivery plan: 117 MW delivered in H1 2026; six data centers under construction (five in the Greater Beijing Area, one in the Yangtze River Delta); about 585 MW to be delivered over the next 12 months - around 333 MW in H2 2026 and around 252 MW in H1 2027 - mostly from the Ulanqab IDC campus. Management expects customers' move-in pace to be faster in H2 2026 than H1, as domestically produced chips ramp up production in H2 2026. Over 90% of wholesale IDC revenue is recurring, with a weighted average remaining lease term of seven years.
quarterly_data.figure: 117 MW delivered in H1 2026; around 333 MW in H2 2026 and around 252 MW in H1 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Demand and supply (management): overall compute demand is trending up from both AI training and inference, with incremental demand largely from leading internet companies procuring high-capacity, high-density cabinets; several major players are expected to issue gigawatt-level tenders in 2026, mainly in the national hubs of the East Data, West Computing Initiative. The sector is in 'a tight equilibrium': the release of effective compute capacity is constrained by power availability, chip supply chains and other bottlenecks, which management sees as a sustained tailwind for VNET. New-project pricing will reflect regional peer rates, construction costs and resource scarcity; existing projects follow contract rates.

VNET signed a strategic cooperation agreement with CATL to jointly develop a three-layer integrated compute-energy ecosystem - gigawatt-scale compute energy facilities, distributed compute-energy networks and a zero-carbon token ecosystem - using green direct-current and direct green power connection technologies. VNET plans to lay out its future operating strategy and outlook to the market in the fourth quarter.

Overseas (management): approximately 500 MW of overseas resources secured; the first overseas project to be delivered will be in Southeast Asia, with the Middle East and Europe under evaluation. VNET will use its own funds only to acquire land and will start mechanical and electrical fit-out only after securing firm customer orders, as overseas construction costs are relatively high. Customer mix: beyond leading internet companies and hyperscalers, VNET is expanding to AI model companies and other high-growth AI companies.
